find_composer.description: Look up one composer by name and get their dates, the period they belong to, a portrait, the kinds of music they wrote, and whether they are among the best known. Use it to turn a name from a form, an email or a spreadsheet into a real composer before the next step asks for their works. A surname is enough, capitals and accents do not matter, and a misspelling comes back with the names it nearly matched rather than with nothing.
find_composer.name: find_composer

parameters.description: Which composer. Pick one from the list, or type a name: a surname ('Beethoven'), a full name ('Ludwig van Beethoven') or a name arriving from an earlier step all work, capitals and accents do not matter, and 'dvorak' finds Dvorak. When a word fits more than one person the closest match is used and the result names who it was, so 'bach' is Johann Sebastian rather than one of his sons.

get_work.description: Get everything the catalogue holds on one piece from its id: the full title, the subtitle, the kind of music, the catalogue number it is known by, whether it is popular or essential, and its composer's dates and portrait. The id comes from any of the other actions, so this is the step after a search or a list when the whole record is wanted.

identify_work.description: Turn the name someone calls a piece by into the real entry for it. It handles the three ways a title is usually written and the catalogue is not: a nickname ('the Moonlight Sonata'), a shorthand ('Symphony no 9'), and the title in another language ('Le sacre du printemps' is filed as The Rite of Spring). Use it to tidy a playlist, a concert listing or a spreadsheet of titles into pieces you can look up.

The three narrow together, so 'the famous Romantics' or 'everyone Baroque under B' is one step rather than three. Use it to build a programme, a quiz, a newsletter series or a picker of your own.

description: Look up classical music from a workflow. Open Opus is a free, hand-curated catalogue of around 220 composers and the works they wrote. Find a composer by name and get their dates, period and portrait; list what they wrote, narrowed to chamber, keyboard, orchestral, stage or vocal music and to the pieces worth hearing; search composers and pieces together when you do not yet know which you have; turn a nickname, a shorthand or a French title into the real entry for a piece; draw suggestions at random for a daily pick or a newsletter; and look up whether a performer conducts, sings or plays an instrument. Composers are picked from a list or typed by name, so nobody has to know that Beethoven is number 145. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
